title: Thanks for the plays, sir!💔 #broadway #westend #theatre #londontheatr...
transcript: we just lost a towering legend of the theatre not only was he one of the greatest playwrights of both the 20th and 21st centuries I also cannot overstate how formative he was for me personally Sir Tom Stoppard is probably most widely known for Rosencrantz and Guildenstern are dead though he did also win an Oscar for the screenplay of Shakespeare in love but my first Broadway play was Arcadia at 15 years old and it changed my brain chemistry and I didn't really understand it but I desperately wanted to because I could tell that it was something very special so I bought a copy of the script and combed through it line by line with a pencil in hand and Google by my side it's by far the most beat up script on my shelf and my efforts were rewarded when I saw another production of the play a couple years later and it emotionally shattered me and to this day I'd still probably say it's my favourite play of all time Stoppard excelled at taking these intellectual academic topics like math, physics, history human consciousness, music theory and infusing them with a deep sense of human emotion or rather finding the emotion that was already in them and as a nerd who's also a Pisces you can only imagine how formative that was for me as I was developing a deeper love for theatre throughout high school and college. he might have even made me more eager to study these subjects in school because through his eyes I could see how inextricably tied to the human experience they were I was 20 years old studying abroad in London when this photo was taken I was in the lobby after one of his shows and my friend Zhe grabbed me by the shoulder and was like “Stoppard is here!” my heart skipped a beat, I was like “where?” and Zhe was like “he's on his way out!” so I bolted to the street just in time to catch him and he was very nice to pose for this photo and listen as I told him how important his work was to me In college I went on to read a bunch of his plays from the 3-part epic Coast of Utopia to more obscure ones like Every Good Boy Deserves Favour and I've been lucky enough to see I think seven of his works live and did I love all of them? no and did some of them work better on the page than they did in live performance? sure but when he was on his game he made me laugh he made me cry and you better f*cking believe he made me think
